reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) supports impurity-driven phase segregation and precipitate formation (α-Ti) during aging, and shows softening from interstitial depletion. However, it does not provide evidence for brittle fracture, reduced toughness, or crack initiation from weak interfaces; these key premises are unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Thermal aging promotes impurity-driven phase segregation in single-phase HEAs
Segregation leads to nucleation of brittle precipitates
Brittle precipitates deplete solid-solution strengthening interstitials
Brittle precipitates introduce weak interfaces that act as crack initiators
This results in reduced toughness and brittle fracture under loading
